nodes.characterization_summary: Pure Ni(OH)₂ shows inhomogeneous microspheres (300-800 nm) of interlaced nanosheets; F-, Cl-, Br-Ni(OH)₂ maintain microspheres with reduced size and thinner nanosheets; I-Ni(OH)₂ exhibits nano-nest structure of ultrathin nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S1a,b, Supporting Information, a scanning electron microscope (SEM) of pure Ni(OH)₂ presents an inhomogeneous microsphere with a diameter of 300 - 800 nm consisting of interlace nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pure Ni(OH)₂: 151.64 m²/g, 10.848 nm pore diameter; Br-Ni(OH)₂: 188.58 m²/g; I-Ni(OH)₂: 229.91 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figures S2 and S3, Supporting Information, the specific surface area and average pore diameter of pure Ni(OH)₂ are 151.64 m² g⁻¹ and 10.848 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples conform to Ni(OH)₂ (JCPDS NO 14-0117); (001) and (100) planes shift to smaller angles with increasing halogen radius, widening layer spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 1e, all characteristic peaks for several samples are conformed to Ni(OH)₂ (JCPDS. NO 14-0117), revealing that the incorporation of individual halogens has a negligible impact on the structural composition of Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: β-Ni-O(H) stretching at 465 and 616 cm⁻¹; F causes shift to lower wavenumber at 465 cm⁻¹; weak band at 310 cm⁻¹ indicates defects; O-H vibration at 995 and 1045 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As presented in Figure 1h, wide bands centered at 465 and 616 cm⁻¹ are typically attributed to the β-Ni-O(H) stretching vibration, revealing its peculiarity of low crystallinity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p₃/₂ shifts from 855.8 eV (pure) to 856.1 eV (F-Ni(OH)₂); F 1s at 683.6 eV confirms Ni-F bond; oxygen vacancy ratios from O 1s fitting: pure Ni(OH)₂ (12.4%), F-Ni(OH)₂ (21.7%), Cl-Ni(OH)₂ (19%), Br-Ni(OH)₂ (16.9%), I-Ni(OH)₂ (17.3%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: By fitting calculation, the ratio of Ov in F-Ni(OH)₂ is 21.7%, which is larger than 19% in Cl-Ni(OH)₂, 16.9% in Br-Ni(OH)₂, 17.3% in I-Ni(OH)₂, and 12.4% in pure Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Halogen content decreases from F to I; O content reduced in I-Ni(OH)₂ due to oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further confirm the content of halogen elements in samples, the results of the energy dispersive X-ray spectrum (EDS) are shown in Table S1, Supporting Information.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pure Ni(OH)₂ shows agglomerated microsphere; F,I-Ni(OH)₂ shows fine nano grains; (002) spacing expands from 0.2302 nm to 0.2408 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM images of pure Ni(OH)₂ shown in Figure 3e present a microsphere consisting of a large number of nanosheets agglomerated irregularly.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bihalogen samples show nearly 1:1 ratio of the two halogens.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron Probe X-ray Micro-Analyzer (EPMA) in Figure S9a-c, Supporting Information, shows that the ratio of the two different halogen ions is almost 1:1 in bihalogen-engineered Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental content quantification shows halogen incorporation in electrode materials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental content of the prepared electrode materials was quantified by EPMA (JXA-8530F Plus).
